component.name: ChatonLM
component.summary: Local AI desktop app: chat, images, voice and dictation

description.p: ChatonLM is a free, open-source desktop app for using large language models on your own computer. Models run in a built-in engine, llama.cpp, on the processor or the graphics card (Vulkan, with optional NVIDIA acceleration): nothing else to install, no account, no telemetry.

ul.li: Chats with history, favorites, attachments, thinking and web search
Model browser for Hugging Face, image generation
Local dictation, read aloud, voice conversations and proofreading, with global shortcuts
Study tab: courses generated by a model on any subject
Interface in English, Spanish and French
Read selected text aloud: a global shortcut (Ctrl+Alt+R suggested) reads the text selected in any application; press it again to stop. Off by default, in Settings › Keyboard shortcuts.
Proofread options: keep the words in their order, automatic formatting, and keep numbers as digits. They also apply to the global shortcut and to VS Code.
Report a bug from Settings › General: your message, an optional reply address and a diagnostic you can read before sending. ChatonLM now keeps a log of its own, which you can open from there.
The database is backed up before each update of its format. If you go back to an older version, ChatonLM offers to restore that backup.
Logging out or shutting down closes ChatonLM cleanly: temporary chats are erased and models are unloaded.
Text copied by dictation and proofreading stays out of the clipboard history, and out of the Windows cloud clipboard.
The model picker shows how much memory a recommended model needs and whether it fits your computer, and says when Ollama can't be reached.
The VS Code link can only read and continue the chats started in VS Code.
The active tab's highlight slides to the new one, switches and sliders are easier to see, and the French voice speaks a little more slowly.
Built-in Ollama updated to 0.40.15.
VS Code link: pair VS Code (or VSCodium) with ChatonLM in Settings › VS Code, then use the ChatonLM for VS Code extension to chat about your code with your local models.

From VS Code: explain, fix and test code, write commit messages, guided tours of the code read aloud, hands-free voice conversations, dictation at the cursor, local autocomplete, image generation, proofreading of comments and documents, and courses on a project in the Study tab.
Easy Link: VS Code can tell your Telegram or Discord bot when a long terminal command ends.
ChatonLM can serve its models to the coding agents of VS Code (MCP), with a separate permission.
ChatonLM plans what fits on the graphics card: the autocomplete model never pushes the chat model out, and waits while a reply or an image is being made.
Proofread: a paragraph broken over several lines keeps its line breaks instead of being left uncorrected.
Built-in Ollama updated to 0.40.13.
Proofread and Study: the new Auto model choice uses the best model already loaded, or the chat model when none is loaded.
Ephemeral chats: click the ghost kitten at the top right; the chat stays out of your history and is erased when you open another chat or quit, unless you keep it. Works from Easy Link too.
Ollama cloud models, optional and off by default (Settings › Models).
Dictation: the text is pasted where the cursor is.
Models still loaded are unloaded when you quit ChatonLM (can be turned off).
Settings › General: choose whether the close button keeps ChatonLM in the system tray or quits it, and a way to support ChatonLM with a donation.
A snail shows when a model runs partly on the processor because graphics memory is short.
Built-in Ollama updated to 0.40.11.

Image generation in the chat: press the Image button, or ask a model that can use tools for a picture. Runs on your computer with a built-in image engine (stable-diffusion.cpp), on the graphics card or, more slowly, on the processor.
ModelHub, Images tab: pick free image models from Hugging Face (FLUX.2 klein, Z-Image and more), with what each one is good at, its speed, the graphics memory it needs and its license.
Easy Link: pictures made by the model are sent to your Telegram or Discord bot.
Context: a gauge shows how full the model's context is; long conversations can be compacted, automatically or on demand.
A model that loops is stopped or flagged.
Settings: a system prompt sent with every chat, and a graphics memory gauge.
ModelHub: an optional Uncensored section, hidden by default.
Easy Link: talk to your models from your own Telegram or Discord bot while ChatonLM runs on your computer (text, photos, voice messages, web search).
First launch: choose your language, then take a short guided tour of the app.
Models: a newer version of an installed model is announced and can be downloaded; downloads can be paused and resumed.
Study: courses can be paused and resumed, and lessons read aloud.
Proofread: the corrected text is pasted in place of the selection.
Built-in Ollama updated to 0.40.3.
